transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-13 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Novus Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Infra), Tom Reed (Product), Maya Li (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, i'm jordan lee, AE at Redwood. we do inference infra and today priya will cover the technical benchmark plan.
[00:18] Carlos: hey jordan, good to be here. quick context - we're building a recommendations assistant inside our trading desk product. typical user flow is prompt + account context, so token sizes can vary. main ask is: can you handle our throughput and keep latencies < 150ms p50 for short responses.
[00:32] Priya: cool, thanks carlos. just to confirm, the main success criteria are latency under 150ms p50, cost target of ~ $0.002 per 1k tokens after batching and caching, and compatibility with our VPC + KMS. is that right?
[00:46] Tom: yes, and also we want to see tail latency behavior p95/p99, and get an estimate for dedicated pricing if this is a long-term match.
[01:02] Jordan: great, we'll scope a 3-week POC, first week baseline, second week stress/scale, third week optimization and handoff.
[01:15] Maya: quick sec — security is critical; we'll need SOC2 and key management details. can you run in our VPC or do you need peering?
[01:28] Priya: we have private deployment options: VPC peering or a private dedicated cluster. we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. we'll share the security pack.
[01:40] Carlos: ok good. on workload: our peak planning is 500 QPS sustained with spikes to 1k QPS for short windows. average concurrency per user session roughly 8 requests/sec? actually — sorry — 8 concurrent sessions during trading hours, maybe i mean 800 concurrent requests across the fleet.
[01:59] Aisha: i'll clarify: typical day avg is 120 QPS, but heavy events push to 700-1k for 10-30m bursts.
[02:10] Priya: great; that's helpful. for the POC we usually ask customers to define several workload slices: baseline (120 QPS, small prompts), peak burst (1k QPS for 15m), and heavy context (longer input token distribution).
[02:28] Jordan: also need to characterize input/output tokens. carlos, what's the median prompt length and median completion length?
[02:36] Carlos: median prompt is 120 tokens, completions are short — 20-40 tokens typically; but some flows use 400-800 token context for risk calculations.
[02:48] Priya: okay so distribution is multi-modal: short prompts (120 in, 30 out) and long-context cases (600 in, 200 out). for modeling we treat them separately because KV cache behavior and memory footprint differs.
[03:05] Tom: what about concurrency per request? do you mean how many requests your runtime can pipeline on a single model host?
[03:12] Priya: yes — concurrency and QPS interplay. we need to simulate average simultaneous open streams and the token generation rate. we'll provide a load generator that can hit QPS and also emulate streaming tokens to capture tail latency.
[03:28] [crosstalk] Speaker 6: mhm, sounds good —
[03:35] Priya: for compute sizing, initial recommendation is start with a 4-gpu dedicated cluster (A40-like or H100 depending on model), tuned for 512k KV cache and batching window of 20-50ms. that should cover 500 QPS with small prompts with room to scale to 1k with autoscaling.
[03:56] Aisha: what's the model size you're assuming? 7b? 13b?
[04:02] Priya: we recommend testing both a 13B and a quantized 70B-llm variant — sorry, i said 70B but meant a 33B quantized. transcription note: sometimes model names get swapped. the idea is to compare a medium-sized open model vs a larger quantized model to analyze cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:24] Carlos: we care most about latency and correctness for short responses. cost is second. so if 13B hits p50<150ms that's the winner.
[04:34] Jordan: noted. i'll include these as explicit success criteria in the SOW.
[04:40] Priya: on measurements we'll report p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, GPU utilization, batching efficiency, KV cache hit rate, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also provide per-route metrics so you can see behavior for each prompt type.
[05:00] Tom: about caching — can you do prefix caching across sessions? our user flow often reuses account-level context.
[05:08] Priya: yes, prefix/KV caching is supported and can reduce compute for repeated context. we'll instrument cache-hit ratios in the benchmark.
[05:16] Maya: security follow-up - do you support customer-managed KMS and audit logs for per-request keys?
[05:24] Jordan: yes, we support CMK integration and detailed audit logs. we'll attach our SOC2 and KMS integration guide.
[05:35] Carlos: good. timeline-wise — when can we run the bench?
[05:39] Jordan: if we get SOW signed within a week, we can schedule the first run the week of 7/20. Priya, can you prep the harness by then?
[05:47] Priya: yes, i'll upload the harness to the shared bucket and include run-book and a k6 load script. it will support QPS ramp, bursts, multi-modal token distributions, and streaming.
[05:59] [10:12] Priya: quick aside on metric collection - we'll run both synthetic microbenchmarks (single host perf) and end-to-end traffic generator to capture autoscaling and routing behavior. synthetic tests give latency floor; traffic generator shows real tail behavior.
[10:30] Aisha: for the staging environment we prefer to run in our cloud account with VPC peering — avoids data egress and simplifies security.
[10:40] Jordan: that works. we have a private deployment flow that supports your cloud account; we'll provide a terraform module to provision endpoints and RBAC.
[11:02] Tom: pricing: can you ballpark dedicated cost for steady 500 QPS?
[11:10] Jordan: rough ballpark: a dedicated 4-GPU pool for 24/7 would be in the mid-five figures per month — we'll provide detailed pricing in the SOW. actual unit cost after batching depends on model and caching; we'll estimate post-benchmark.
[11:28] Carlos: sounds fine. we need to define the POC success criteria clearly. propose: 1) p50 < 150ms on baseline slice, 2) p95 < 400ms, 3) cost <= target TBD after bench but under our internal threshold, 4) deployable in our VPC with KMS and audit logs.
[11:48] Priya: agree. we'll also add completion quality checks — a sample prompt set for QA to ensure output quality doesn't regress.
[12:00] Maya: and security sign-off for KMS/peering.
[12:06] Jordan: we'll add that to success matrix.
[12:10] [15:02] Priya: going into specifics of the load model - we'll param: QPS schedule (baseline, peak spike), concurrency targets, token distribution (short/long/very long), and L7 routing mix (70% short prompts, 20% long context, 10% streaming). we'll include JSON config for the load generator.
[15:34] Carlos: can the harness replay real user prompts with variable user context? we can export a sanitized sample.
[15:42] Priya: yes, the harness supports replay and randomized context IDs to exercise cache hits. please sanitize PII before sharing.
[15:55] Aisha: note on networking: we need mutual TLS and private DNS. can you support that?
[16:02] Jordan: yes — we support mTLS and private DNS endpoints. we'll document required firewall rules.
[16:12] Tom: what's the expected failure mode under saturation? do you shed load or queue?
[16:20] Priya: by policy we can return graceful degradation: fallback to a smaller model, or queue with informative error. we'll include autoscaling policies to handle spikes; for strict SLAs, dedicated reserve is recommended.
[16:36] [20:00] Carlos: for the benchmark outputs, can you include cost modeling per 1m tokens and sensitivity to batching window?
[20:08] Priya: absolutely — we'll vary batching windows (20ms, 50ms, 100ms) and show throughput/latency/cost curves. quantization profiles too.
[20:20] Jordan: ok next steps recap — Jordan sends SOW + pricing, Priya uploads harness, Novus provisions staging VPC, Maya sends security questionnaire answers. schedule run week of 7/20.
[20:40] Tom: agreed. one more ask: we'd like per-request tracing so we can map application latency to model latency. do you expose tracing hooks?
[20:49] Priya: yes, we emit per-request traces and have integration with Jaeger/Zipkin and OpenTelemetry. we'll include a tracing example and dashboard config.
[21:05] [25:00] Maya: i'll need a list of logs retained and how to access audit logs for compliance.
[25:10] Jordan: we'll include retention policies and options in the security pack.
[25:22] Carlos: any gotchas on tokenization differences across models? sometimes token counts vary and affect cost.
[25:31] Priya: good point — we'll run tokenizer parity checks as part of pre-bench to normalize token counting across model candidates.
[25:45] Aisha: do you run any warm-up sequences to populate KV caches before measuring?
[25:52] Priya: yes, benchmarks include warm-up phases (10-15 minutes) and we'll report before/after cache hit ratios.
[26:05] Jordan: okay looks like we have alignment. i'll get the SOW out today.
[26:12] Carlos: thanks jordan and priya. excited to move forward.
[26:18] [30:00] Priya: i'll also include a template for the success criteria matrix so we can sign-off quickly.
[30:12] Tom: thanks. wrapping up — scheduled follow-up to review bench week of 7/27.
[30:22] Jordan: perfect. action items in the notes. thanks everyone.
[30:30] End of recording.
